advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Defer/avoid the `rebar._store.fsutil` import so `--check` does not trigger the whole `rebar.__init__` import chain (import inside `write_baseline`, or vendor the tiny atomic-write into the script).
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:77-82: `# ``fsutil`` is a stdlib-only leaf; ...` then `from rebar._store.fsutil import atomic_write  # noqa: E402`
src/rebar/__init__.py:27-28: `from rebar import config` / `from rebar._engine import engine_dir` — executed whenever any rebar submodule is imported

`_run_check` (scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:419-429) never uses `atomic_write`, yet the gate is wired into `make lint` (Makefile:158) and both CI lanes; an import-time failure anywhere in `rebar.__init__` would break the complexity gate.
advisory.finding: Importing `from rebar._store.fsutil import atomic_write` at module top-level executes `rebar/__init__.py` (which imports `rebar.config`, `rebar._engine`, and `importlib.metadata`), so even `--check` mode — where `atomic_write` is never called — is coupled to the entire rebar package import surface; the 'stdlib-only leaf' comment is misleading because importing the submodule still runs the package __init__ first.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move `from rebar._store.fsutil import atomic_write` (and the sys.path insertion) into `write_baseline`/`_run_update_stale` so only the mutating `--update-stale` path pays the import cost, keeping `--check` decoupled from rebar package import side effects.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the ambiguity tie-break to compare against Ruff's reported `def`-keyword column (`child.col_offset + 1`) rather than the function-name column, or key the index on the `def` column.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:182-183: `keyword_len = 10 if ... AsyncFunctionDef else 4` / `name_col = child.col_offset + keyword_len + 1`
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:205-208: tie-break `exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]`

Ticket census sample: for a 4-space-indented method `location.column` = 5 while AST `col_offset` = 4 (Ruff reports the `def` keyword column, not the name); computed name_col would be 9, never equal to Ruff's 5.
advisory.finding: `build_symbol_index` computes `name_col` as the function-NAME column (`col_offset + keyword_len + 1`), but Ruff's C901 `location.column` points at the `def`/`async` keyword, so the ambiguity tie-break in `resolve_symbol` can never match — two `FunctionDef`s on the same physical line would always raise NormalizationError instead of being disambiguated by column.
advisory.suggested_fix: Set `name_col = child.col_offset + 1` (the 1-based column of the `def`/`async` keyword, matching Ruff's `location.column`) so the tie-break in `resolve_symbol` can actually match.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that resolves two functions sharing one source line by column (and one asserting the ambiguous-resolution NormalizationError), covering the async/def name-column arithmetic.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:205-208: `exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]` ... `raise NormalizationError(f"ambiguous function definition at line {row}, column {column}")`
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:182-183: `keyword_len = 10 if isinstance(child, ast.AsyncFunctionDef) else 4` / `name_col = child.col_offset + keyword_len + 1`

Test helper `_finding` always sets `"location": {"row": row, "column": 1}` and all resolve_symbol calls pass column=0 (test_resolve_* helpers), so the `name_col == column` branch is never satisfied with a real column and the ambiguous-failure branch is never hit.
ABSENCE: no test constructs two functions on the same source line disambiguated by the Ruff column, nor asserts the ambiguous-resolution NormalizationError.
advisory.finding: The column-based symbol disambiguation path in resolve_symbol (and the name-column arithmetic in build_symbol_index) is never exercised: all tests resolve with column=0 and _finding() hardcodes column=1, so neither the correct-of-two same-line resolution nor the 'ambiguous function definition' NormalizationError is tested. A regression in the `child.col_offset + keyword_len + 1` arithmetic (e.g. wrong async/def offset) would resolve the wrong qualified symbol undetected.

test_update_stale_refuses_on_scanner_error and test_update_stale_refuses_on_schema_error cover the update-stale side, but the only _run_check tests (test_run_check_reports_regression, test_run_check_allows_stale) inject clean run_scanner/normalize_findings and never raise a BaselineError.

advisory.finding: _run_check's error branch (BaselineError -> print 'error:' -> return 1) is untested, unlike the symmetric _run_update_stale scanner/schema-error tests. No test injects a ScannerError or SchemaError into _run_check to confirm the gate exits nonzero (rather than passing) on a scanner or baseline-schema failure.
